# 1 Enoch Chapter 72 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn-astr (Aramaic) | **Section:** Astronomical Book (Book of Luminaries)

---

**1** The book of the courses of the luminaries of heaven — their relations to one another, their classes, their dominion and their seasons, their names and places of origin, and their months — which Uriel, the holy angel who was with me and who is their guide, showed to me. He showed me all their laws exactly as they are, and how it is with every year of the world unto eternity, until the new creation that shall endure forever is accomplished.

**2** This is the first law of the luminaries: the luminary the Sun has its rising in the eastern portals of heaven and its setting in the western portals of heaven.

**3** I saw six portals in which the sun rises, and six portals in which the sun sets; and the moon rises and sets in these same portals, as do the leaders of the stars and those they lead — six in the east and six in the west — all following one another in precisely corresponding order. And there are many windows to the right and left of these portals.

**4** First goes forth the great luminary called the Sun, and his circuit runs like the circuit of heaven; he proceeds westward for one hundred and eighty days and sets in the west.

**5** In those days the day grows longer and the night grows shorter, so that the day is longer than the night by a tenth part.

**6** The day is exactly ten parts and the night is eight parts.

**7** The sun rises from the third portal, proceeds and sets in the third portal in the west, goes forth for thirty-one days, and then sets in the second portal.

**8** In those days the night grows longer and the day grows shorter, until the thirtieth morning arrives, when the day is exactly ten parts and the night is eight parts.

**9** At the setting of the sun the ruler of the night begins his course. In those days the night grows longer and the day grows shorter.

**10** In those days the night is exactly nine parts and the day is nine parts — the night is equal to the day.

**11** The night is exactly nine parts and the day nine parts.

**12** In those days the sun rises from that portal and sets in the west, returns to the east, and rises in the fourth portal for thirty-one mornings, then sets in the west of heaven.

**13** In those days the day grows longer day by day and the night grows shorter night by night until the thirtieth morning.

**14** In those days the day becomes ten parts and the night eight parts.

**15** The sun rises from that portal and sets in the fifth portal in the west for thirty days, then rises in the fifth portal and sets in the fifth portal in the west.

**16** In those days the day grows longer and the night shorter, until the day is eleven parts and the night seven parts.

**17** The sun returns to the east and enters the sixth portal, and rises and sets in the sixth portal for thirty-one days according to its sign.

**18** In those days the day grows longer than the night; the day becomes double the night; the day becomes twelve parts and the night six parts.

**19** The sun rises such that the day is shortened and the night lengthened; the sun returns to the east and enters the sixth portal, and rises and sets in the sixth portal for thirty days.

**20** In those days the day grows shorter and the night grows longer; in thirty days the day is ten parts and the night eight parts.

**21** The sun goes forth from the sixth portal and sets in the west, then proceeds to the east and rises in the fifth portal for thirty days, then sets in the west again.

**22** In those days the day is eleven parts and the night seven parts.

**23** The sun goes forth from the fifth portal and sets in the fifth portal in the west, then rises in the fourth portal for thirty-one days according to its sign, and sets in the west.

**24** In those days the day becomes equal to the night — they are equal — the night is nine parts and the day nine parts.

**25** The sun rises from the fourth portal and sets in the fourth portal, returns to the east, and rises in the third portal for thirty-one mornings, then sets in the west of heaven.

**26** In those days the night grows longer than the day; the night becomes double the day; the night becomes ten parts and the day eight parts.

**27** The sun rises from the third portal and sets in the third portal in the west, returns to the east, and rises for thirty mornings in the second portal of the east, then sets in the second portal of heaven in the west.

**28** In those days the night becomes eleven parts and the day seven parts.

**29** The sun returns to the east and enters the first portal, and sets for thirty-one mornings in the west in the first portal of heaven.

**30** In those days the night grows longer and reaches double the day; the night becomes twelve parts and the day six parts.

**31** The sun has traversed the divisions of its course and turns again upon those divisions; it enters that portal for thirty mornings and sets in the west opposite to it.

**32** In that night the night decreases in length by a ninth part; the night is eleven parts and the day seven parts.

**33** The sun returns and enters the second portal in the east, and continues on these divisions of its course for thirty mornings, rising and setting.

**34** In those days the night decreases in length; the night is nine parts and the day nine parts, and the night is equal to the day.

**35** And the year is exactly three hundred and sixty-four days.

**36** The length of the day and of the night, and the shortness of the day and of the night, differ from each other because of the sun's journey — these differences arise from it.

**37** So it comes about that its journey becomes daily longer and its journey nightly shorter, by reason of the sun and by reason of its portals.

---

*LOGOS notes: Formal equivalence rendering from the Ge'ez text, preserving sentence structure and key theological vocabulary while producing readable English prose. The 364-day solar calendar described here stood in deliberate contrast to the 354-day lunar calendar. This calendar is foundational for the Qumran community's liturgical schedule.*
